newsitem.title: UGANDA: Drought to cut Ugandan 1997 tea production.
newsitem.headline: Drought to cut Ugandan 1997 tea production.

text.p: Drought in the first quarter of the year will push Uganda's tea production significantly below the 1997 total of 17,000 tonnes, growers said on Thursday.
David Kimpwitu, chairman of the Uganda Tea Association, told Reuters that effects of drought were very serious, especially for smallholders responsible for most of Uganda's tea.
He would not give any specific figures.
"The drought had a very serious effect. The crop dropped drastically," Kimpwitu told Reuters.
Using figures from Uganda Tea Growers Corporation (UTGC), Kimpwitu said tea production had more than halved in March compared to January.
UTGC has a grower membership of 11,000 and accounts for half of Uganda's total production. UTGC production in March was 166 tonnes compared to 421 tonnes in January and 235 in February.
But industry officials said increased demand had forced up prices for Ugandan tea to $1.45 per kg (2.2 lbs) from $1.16 this time last year.
Kimpwitu said seasonal long rains, which arrived in Uganda late last month, had given an indication that tea production would improve -- but damage was already significant.
UTGC accounts for 9,441 hectares of Uganda's total 20,500 hectares under tea.
